{{nihongo|'''Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto'''|天社土御門神道}}<ref>https://archive.today/uJNu5</ref> is a form of [[Confucian Shinto]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Encyclopedia of Shinto詳細 |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8943 |access-date=2023-03-10 |website=國學院大學デジタルミュージアム |language=ja}}</ref> It is also known as Tsuchimikado Shinto
It was founded by [[Abe no Seimei]] and influenced by [[:en:Onmyodo|Onmyodo]].<ref name="國學院大學テシタルミューシアム-2023a">{{Cite web |title=Encyclopedia of Shinto詳細 |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9907 |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=國學院大學デジタルミュージアム |language=ja}}</ref> in the 900s<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Cali |first1=Joseph |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=J1gEEAAAQBAJ&dq=tsuchimikado+shinto&pg=PA137 |title=Shinto Shrines: A Guide to the Sacred Sites of Japan's Ancient Religion |last2=Dougill |first2=John |date=30 November 2012 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-3775-4 |language=en}}</ref> It is highly linked to the [[Abe clan]].<ref name="國學院大學テシタルミューシアム-2023a" />
It is considered the modern form of Onmyodo.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Makoto |first=Hayashi |last2=Luers |first2=Dylan |last3=林淳 |date=2013 |title=The Development of Early Modern Onmyōdō |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/41955534 |journal=Japanese Journal of Religious Studies |volume=40 |issue=1 |pages=151–167 |issn=0304-1042}}</ref>
The current head is Yoshihito Fujita<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 October 2015 |title=天社土御門神道本庁 |url=https://japanese-religions.com/jr4210005008880/ |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=JAPANESE RELIGIONS |language=ja}}</ref>
It was banned by the {{interlanguage link|Tensha Shinto Prohibition Ordinance|ja|天社禁止令}}
Tsuchimikado Shintō was abolished in 1870 with the ban of [[Onmyōdō]], and only permitted again in 1945 with religious freedom and the abolition of [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]].<ref name="國學院大學テシタルミューシアム-2023a" /> A new organization was created for it in 1954.<ref>{{Cite web |title=備忘録 天社土御門神道 本庁 |url=http://kashomemorandum.blog.fc2.com/blog-entry-137.html |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=kashomemorandum.blog.fc2.com}}</ref>

== Historical Background == The origins of Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto trace back to the [[Abe clan|Abe family]]'s establishment of Onmyōdō as a hereditary discipline focusing on {{ill|Astronomy|ja|天文道|1=Tenmondō (astrology)|lt=Tenmondō|qq= (astrology)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Astronomy|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmondō (astrology)|qq=}}, {{ill|Calendar Science|ja|暦道|1=Rekidō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Calendar Science|13=User:Immanuelle/Rekidō|qq=}}, and [[:en:Onmyōdō|Onmyōdō]] during the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]]. The family name "Tsuchimikado" was adopted after {{ill|Abe no Ariyo|ja|安倍有世|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe no Ariyo|qq=}} was granted the extraordinary court Rank of Junior Second Rank by [[:en:Ashikaga Yoshimitsu|Ashikaga Yoshimitsu]]. During the [[:en:Ōnin War|Ōnin War]], the family evacuated their estates in Kyoto and relocated to the Nata-shō area in [[:en:Wakasa Province|Wakasa Province]], where they were su11orted by local warlords such as the {{ill|Wakasa Takeda clan|ja|若狭武田氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakasa Takeda clan|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武田氏|1=Takeda clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1210114}}.
Despite this relocation, much of the Onmyōdō knowledge and practices maintained by the {{ill|Onmyōryō|ja|陰陽寮|1=Yin-Yang Bureau|2=ja|3=陰陽寮|4=fr|5=Bureau d'Onmyō|6=zh|7=阴阳寮|8=ko|9=음양료|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyōryō|13=User:Immanuelle/Yin-Yang Bureau|qq=}} were lost during the [[:en:Ōnin War|Ōnin War]]. Efforts were made to recover elements of Onmyōdō by incorporating practices from [[:en:Yoshida Shintō|Yoshida Shinto]] and elements influenced by esoteric Buddhism.
== Development into Tensha Shinto == Through the leadership of {{ill|Tsuchimikado Taifuku|ja|土御門泰福|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado Taifuku|1=Tsuchimikado Yasutomi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11423487}}, Tensha Shinto emerged as a synthesis of Onmyōdō, Yoshida Shinto practices, and Suika Shinto's Confucian-based teachings. Taifuku was a disciple of [[:en:Yamazaki Ansai|Yamazaki Ansai]], who emphasized reverence for the imperial lineage and divine sovereignty.
== Post-Meiji Restoration and Revival == With the [[Meiji Restoration]], Onmyōdō and Tensha Shinto were banned under the {{ill|Decree Prohibiting Tensha|ja|天社禁止令|1=Tensha Shinto Prohibition Ordinance|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Decree Prohibiting Tensha|13=User:Immanuelle/Tensha Shinto Prohibition Ordinance|qq=}} in 1870. The Tsuchimikado family ceased to engage in Onmyōdō practices, and the Tensha Shinto organization faced dissolution.
The revival of Tensha Shinto began in [[:en:Shōwa era|Shōwa period]] 29 (1954) with its incorporation as a religious corporation. Its headquarters was established in Fukui Prefecture, and the Fujita family assumed leadership roles.
== Current Status == Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto currently operates under the leadership of Fujita Yoshihito. The organization oversees several affiliated shrines and religious institutions. Efforts have been made to promote Tensha Shinto as part of local cultural heritage, su11orted by collaborations between academia, local governments, and private enterprises.

'''Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto''' (天社土御門神道, Tensha Tsuchimikado Shintō), or simply '''Tsuchimikado Shinto''' (土御門神道, Tsuchimikado Shintō), is a [[:en:Religious organization|Religious organization]] headquartered in [[Ōi Town]], [[Ōi District]], [[:en:Fukui Prefecture|Fukui Prefecture]] (formerly Nata-shō Village). The name "Tsuchimikado Shinto" is generally used, but it is also referred to as "Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto," incorporating the term "Tensha" from "Tensha Shrine" (天社宮), a shrine name bestowed by [[:en:Reigen Emperor|Reigen Emperor]] upon the Tsuchimikado family during the Edo period as the "Soke of Onmyōdō."
Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto is rooted in the [[Onmyōdō]] (yin-yang way) traditions passed down by the {{ill|Abe clan|ja|安倍氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe clan|qq=}}'s {{ill|Tsuchimikado clan|lt=Tsuchimikado clan|lt=Tsuchimikado family|ja|土御門家|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado family|qq=}}, descendants of [[Abe no Seimei]]. However, it evolved into "Tensha Shinto" by incorporating influences from [[:en:Yoshida Shinto|Yoshida Shinto]] in the medieval period and [[Suika Shinto]] proposed by the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] Shintoist and Confucian scholar [[:en:Yamazaki Ansai|Yamazaki Ansai]]. Strictly speaking, it is no longer purely Onmyōdō but is considered a Shinto-based organization{{efn2|While it is classified under "Miscellaneous Religions" in the religious corporation registry and not under [[:en:Sect Shinto|Sect Shinto]] or [[:en:Shrine Shinto|Shrine Shinto]].<ref name="nisino">[[#nisino|Nishino Shrine Journal]]</ref>}}. Currently, its leadership does not reside with the head of the Tsuchimikado family but rather with the Fujita family, which historically managed the household affairs of the Tsuchimikado family.
After the last Tsuchimikado family head, {{ill|Tsuchimikado Noriitada|ja|土御門範忠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado Noriitada|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135491517}} (1920–1994), passed away, the position of "Chief Priest" was abolished. Media and public relations are handled under the title "Leader of Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto Honcho" (庁長) or simply "Representative." The current highest-Ranking official (representative of the organization) holds the title "Honcho Leader."

== Historical Background == The origins of Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto trace back to the [[Abe clan|Abe family]]'s establishment of Onmyōdō as a hereditary discipline focusing on {{ill|Astronomy|ja|天文道|1=Tenmondō (astrology)|lt=Tenmondō|qq= (astrology)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Astronomy|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmondō (astrology)|qq=}}, {{ill|Calendar Science|ja|暦道|1=Rekidō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Calendar Science|13=User:Immanuelle/Rekidō|qq=}}, and [[:en:Onmyōdō|Onmyōdō]] during the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]]. The family name "Tsuchimikado" was adopted after {{ill|Abe no Ariyo|ja|安倍有世|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe no Ariyo|qq=}} was granted the extraordinary court Rank of Junior Second Rank by [[:en:Ashikaga Yoshimitsu|Ashikaga Yoshimitsu]]. During the [[:en:Ōnin War|Ōnin War]], the family evacuated their estates in Kyoto and relocated to the Nata-shō area in [[:en:Wakasa Province|Wakasa Province]], where they were su11orted by local warlords such as the {{ill|Wakasa Takeda clan|ja|若狭武田氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakasa Takeda clan|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武田氏|1=Takeda clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1210114}}.
Despite this relocation, much of the Onmyōdō knowledge and practices maintained by the {{ill|Onmyōryō|ja|陰陽寮|1=Yin-Yang Bureau|2=ja|3=陰陽寮|4=fr|5=Bureau d'Onmyō|6=zh|7=阴阳寮|8=ko|9=음양료|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyōryō|13=User:Immanuelle/Yin-Yang Bureau|qq=}} were lost during the [[:en:Ōnin War|Ōnin War]]. Efforts were made to recover elements of Onmyōdō by incorporating practices from [[:en:Yoshida Shintō|Yoshida Shinto]] and elements influenced by esoteric Buddhism.
== Development into Tensha Shinto == Through the leadership of {{ill|Tsuchimikado Taifuku|ja|土御門泰福|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado Taifuku|1=Tsuchimikado Yasutomi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11423487}}, Tensha Shinto emerged as a synthesis of Onmyōdō, Yoshida Shinto practices, and Suika Shinto's Confucian-based teachings. Taifuku was a disciple of [[:en:Yamazaki Ansai|Yamazaki Ansai]], who emphasized reverence for the imperial lineage and divine sovereignty.
== Post-Meiji Restoration and Revival == With the [[Meiji Restoration]], Onmyōdō and Tensha Shinto were banned under the {{ill|Decree Prohibiting Tensha|ja|天社禁止令|1=Tensha Shinto Prohibition Ordinance|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Decree Prohibiting Tensha|13=User:Immanuelle/Tensha Shinto Prohibition Ordinance|qq=}} in 1870. The Tsuchimikado family ceased to engage in Onmyōdō practices, and the Tensha Shinto organization faced dissolution.
The revival of Tensha Shinto began in [[:en:Shōwa era|Shōwa period]] 29 (1954) with its incorporation as a religious corporation. Its headquarters was established in Fukui Prefecture, and the Fujita family assumed leadership roles.
== Current Status == Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto currently operates under the leadership of Fujita Yoshihito. The organization oversees several affiliated shrines and religious institutions. Efforts have been made to promote Tensha Shinto as part of local cultural heritage, su11orted by collaborations between academia, local governments, and private enterprises.

'''Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto''' (天社土御門神道, Tensha Tsuchimikado Shintō), or simply '''Tsuchimikado Shinto''' (土御門神道, Tsuchimikado Shintō), is a [[:en:Religious organization|Religious organization]] headquartered in [[Ōi Town]], [[Ōi District]], [[:en:Fukui Prefecture|Fukui Prefecture]] (formerly Nata-shō Village). The name "Tsuchimikado Shinto" is generally used, but it is also referred to as "Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto," incorporating the term "Tensha" from "Tensha Shrine" (天社宮), a shrine name bestowed by [[:en:Reigen Emperor|Reigen Emperor]] upon the Tsuchimikado family during the Edo period as the "Soke of Onmyōdō."
Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto is rooted in the [[Onmyōdō]] (yin-yang way) traditions passed down by the {{ill|Abe clan|ja|安倍氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe clan|qq=}}'s {{ill|Tsuchimikado clan|lt=Tsuchimikado clan|lt=Tsuchimikado family|ja|土御門家|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado family|qq=}}, descendants of [[Abe no Seimei]]. However, it evolved into "Tensha Shinto" by incorporating influences from [[:en:Yoshida Shinto|Yoshida Shinto]] in the medieval period and [[Suika Shinto]] proposed by the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] Shintoist and Confucian scholar [[:en:Yamazaki Ansai|Yamazaki Ansai]]. Strictly speaking, it is no longer purely Onmyōdō but is considered a Shinto-based organization{{efn2|While it is classified under "Miscellaneous Religions" in the religious corporation registry and not under [[:en:Sect Shinto|Sect Shinto]] or [[:en:Shrine Shinto|Shrine Shinto]].<ref name="nisino">[[#nisino|Nishino Shrine Journal]]</ref>}}. Currently, its leadership does not reside with the head of the Tsuchimikado family but rather with the Fujita family, which historically managed the household affairs of the Tsuchimikado family.
After the last Tsuchimikado family head, {{ill|Tsuchimikado Noriitada|ja|土御門範忠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado Noriitada|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135491517}} (1920–1994), passed away, the position of "Chief Priest" was abolished. Media and public relations are handled under the title "Leader of Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto Honcho" (庁長) or simply "Representative." The current highest-Ranking official (representative of the organization) holds the title "Honcho Leader."

The family name "Tsuchimikado" was adopted after {{ill|Abe no Ariyo|ja|安倍有世|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe no Ariyo|qq=}} was granted the extraordinary court Rank of Junior Second Rank by [[:en:Ashikaga Yoshimitsu|Ashikaga Yoshimitsu]]. During the [[:en:Ōnin War|Ōnin War]], the family evacuated their estates in Kyoto and relocated to the Nata-shō area in [[:en:Wakasa Province|Wakasa Province]], where they were su11orted by local warlords such as the {{ill|Wakasa Takeda clan|ja|若狭武田氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakasa Takeda clan|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武田氏|1=Takeda clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1210114}}.

'''Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto''' (天社土御門神道, Tensha Tsuchimikado Shintō), or simply '''Tsuchimikado Shinto''' (土御門神道, Tsuchimikado Shintō), is a [[:en:Religious organization|Religious organization]] headquartered in [[Ōi Town]], [[Ōi District]], [[:en:Fukui Prefecture|Fukui Prefecture]] (formerly Nata-shō Village). The name "Tsuchimikado Shinto" is generally used, but it is also referred to as "Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto," incorporating the term "Tensha" from "Tensha Shrine" (天社宮), a shrine name bestowed by [[:en:Reigen Emperor|Reigen Emperor]] upon the Tsuchimikado family during the Edo period as the "Soke of Onmyōdō."
Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto is rooted in the [[Onmyōdō]] (yin-yang way) traditions passed down by the {{ill|Abe clan|ja|安倍氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe clan|qq=}}'s {{ill|Tsuchimikado clan|lt=Tsuchimikado clan|lt=Tsuchimikado family|ja|土御門家|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado family|qq=}}, descendants of [[Abe no Seimei]]. However, it evolved into "Tensha Shinto" by incorporating influences from [[:en:Yoshida Shinto|Yoshida Shinto]] in the medieval period and [[Suika Shinto]] proposed by the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] Shintoist and Confucian scholar [[:en:Yamazaki Ansai|Yamazaki Ansai]]. Strictly speaking, it is no longer purely Onmyōdō but is considered a Shinto-based organization{{efn2|While it is classified under "Miscellaneous Religions" in the religious corporation registry and not under [[:en:Sect Shinto|Sect Shinto]] or [[:en:Shrine Shinto|Shrine Shinto]].<ref name="nisino">[[#nisino|Nishino Shrine Journal]]</ref>}}. Currently, its leadership does not reside with the head of the Tsuchimikado family but rather with the Fujita family, which historically managed the household affairs of the Tsuchimikado family.
After the last Tsuchimikado family head, {{ill|Tsuchimikado Noriitada|ja|土御門範忠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado Noriitada|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135491517}} (1920–1994), passed away, the position of "Chief Priest" was abolished. Media and public relations are handled under the title "Leader of Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto Honcho" (庁長) or simply "Representative." The current highest-Ranking official (representative of the organization) holds the title "Honcho Leader."

It is considered the modern form of Onmyodo.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Makoto |first=Hayashi |last2=Luers |first2=Dylan |last3=林淳 |date=2013 |title=The Development of Early Modern Onmyōdō |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/41955534 |journal=Japanese Journal of Religious Studies |volume=40 |issue=1 |pages=151–167 |issn=0304-1042}}</ref>
The current head is Yoshihito Fujita<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 October 2015 |title=天社土御門神道本庁 |url=https://japanese-religions.com/jr4210005008880/ |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=JAPANESE RELIGIONS |language=ja}}</ref>
It was banned by the {{interlanguage link|Tensha Shinto Prohibition Ordinance|ja|天社禁止令}}
Tsuchimikado Shintō was abolished in 1870 with the ban of [[Onmyōdō]], and only permitted again in 1945 with religious freedom and the abolition of [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]].<ref name="國學院大學テシタルミューシアム-2023a" /> A new organization was created for it in 1954.<ref>{{Cite web |title=備忘録 天社土御門神道 本庁 |url=http://kashomemorandum.blog.fc2.com/blog-entry-137.html |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=kashomemorandum.blog.fc2.com}}</ref>
==References== {{reflist}} {{Religious Confucianism}}
== Historical Background == The origins of Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto trace back to the [[Abe clan|Abe family]]'s establishment of Onmyōdō as a hereditary discipline focusing on {{ill|Astronomy|ja|天文道|1=Tenmondō (astrology)|lt=Tenmondō|qq= (astrology)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Astronomy|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmondō (astrology)|qq=}}, {{ill|Calendar Science|ja|暦道|1=Rekidō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Calendar Science|13=User:Immanuelle/Rekidō|qq=}}, and [[:en:Onmyōdō|Onmyōdō]] during the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]]. The family name "Tsuchimikado" was adopted after {{ill|Abe no Ariyo|ja|安倍有世|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe no Ariyo|qq=}} was granted the extraordinary court Rank of Junior Second Rank by [[:en:Ashikaga Yoshimitsu|Ashikaga Yoshimitsu]]. During the [[:en:Ōnin War|Ōnin War]], the family evacuated their estates in Kyoto and relocated to the Nata-shō area in [[:en:Wakasa Province|Wakasa Province]], where they were su11orted by local warlords such as the {{ill|Wakasa Takeda clan|ja|若狭武田氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakasa Takeda clan|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武田氏|1=Takeda clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1210114}}.
Despite this relocation, much of the Onmyōdō knowledge and practices maintained by the {{ill|Onmyōryō|ja|陰陽寮|1=Yin-Yang Bureau|2=ja|3=陰陽寮|4=fr|5=Bureau d'Onmyō|6=zh|7=阴阳寮|8=ko|9=음양료|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyōryō|13=User:Immanuelle/Yin-Yang Bureau|qq=}} were lost during the [[:en:Ōnin War|Ōnin War]]. Efforts were made to recover elements of Onmyōdō by incorporating practices from [[:en:Yoshida Shintō|Yoshida Shinto]] and elements influenced by esoteric Buddhism.
== Development into Tensha Shinto == Through the leadership of {{ill|Tsuchimikado Taifuku|ja|土御門泰福|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado Taifuku|1=Tsuchimikado Yasutomi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11423487}}, Tensha Shinto emerged as a synthesis of Onmyōdō, Yoshida Shinto practices, and Suika Shinto's Confucian-based teachings. Taifuku was a disciple of [[:en:Yamazaki Ansai|Yamazaki Ansai]], who emphasized reverence for the imperial lineage and divine sovereignty.
== Post-Meiji Restoration and Revival == With the [[Meiji Restoration]], Onmyōdō and Tensha Shinto were banned under the {{ill|Decree Prohibiting Tensha|ja|天社禁止令|1=Tensha Shinto Prohibition Ordinance|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Decree Prohibiting Tensha|13=User:Immanuelle/Tensha Shinto Prohibition Ordinance|qq=}} in 1870. The Tsuchimikado family ceased to engage in Onmyōdō practices, and the Tensha Shinto organization faced dissolution.
The revival of Tensha Shinto began in [[:en:Shōwa era|Shōwa period]] 29 (1954) with its incorporation as a religious corporation. Its headquarters was established in Fukui Prefecture, and the Fujita family assumed leadership roles.
== Current Status == Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto currently operates under the leadership of Fujita Yoshihito. The organization oversees several affiliated shrines and religious institutions. Efforts have been made to promote Tensha Shinto as part of local cultural heritage, su11orted by collaborations between academia, local governments, and private enterprises.

'''Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto''' (天社土御門神道, Tensha Tsuchimikado Shintō), or simply '''Tsuchimikado Shinto''' (土御門神道, Tsuchimikado Shintō), is a [[:en:Religious organization|Religious organization]] headquartered in [[Ōi Town]], [[Ōi District]], [[:en:Fukui Prefecture|Fukui Prefecture]] (formerly Nata-shō Village). The name "Tsuchimikado Shinto" is generally used, but it is also referred to as "Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto," incorporating the term "Tensha" from "Tensha Shrine" (天社宮), a shrine name bestowed by [[:en:Reigen Emperor|Reigen Emperor]] upon the Tsuchimikado family during the Edo period as the "Soke of Onmyōdō."
Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto is rooted in the [[Onmyōdō]] (yin-yang way) traditions passed down by the {{ill|Abe clan|ja|安倍氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe clan|qq=}}'s {{ill|Tsuchimikado clan|lt=Tsuchimikado clan|lt=Tsuchimikado family|ja|土御門家|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado family|qq=}}, descendants of [[Abe no Seimei]]. However, it evolved into "Tensha Shinto" by incorporating influences from [[:en:Yoshida Shinto|Yoshida Shinto]] in the medieval period and [[Suika Shinto]] proposed by the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] Shintoist and Confucian scholar [[:en:Yamazaki Ansai|Yamazaki Ansai]]. Strictly speaking, it is no longer purely Onmyōdō but is considered a Shinto-based organization{{efn2|While it is classified under "Miscellaneous Religions" in the religious corporation registry and not under [[:en:Sect Shinto|Sect Shinto]] or [[:en:Shrine Shinto|Shrine Shinto]].<ref name="nisino">[[#nisino|Nishino Shrine Journal]]</ref>}}. Currently, its leadership does not reside with the head of the Tsuchimikado family but rather with the Fujita family, which historically managed the household affairs of the Tsuchimikado family.
After the last Tsuchimikado family head, {{ill|Tsuchimikado Noriitada|ja|土御門範忠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado Noriitada|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135491517}} (1920–1994), passed away, the position of "Chief Priest" was abolished. Media and public relations are handled under the title "Leader of Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto Honcho" (庁長) or simply "Representative." The current highest-Ranking official (representative of the organization) holds the title "Honcho Leader."

After the last Tsuchimikado family head, {{ill|Tsuchimikado Noriitada|ja|土御門範忠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado Noriitada|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135491517}} (1920–1994), passed away, the position of "Chief Priest" was abolished. The current highest-Ranking official (representative of the organization) holds the title "Honcho Leader."

{{Short description|Shinto religious organization}} {{Use dmy dates|date=December 2023}}
{{Infobox organization | name = Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto | founder = [[Abe no Seimei]] | founding_location = Japan | website = https://onmyodo.jp }}
{{nihongo|'''Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto'''|天社土御門神道}}<ref>https://archive.today/uJNu5</ref> is a form of [[Confucian Shinto]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Encyclopedia of Shinto詳細 |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8943 |access-date=2023-03-10 |website=國學院大學デジタルミュージアム |language=ja}}</ref> It is also known as Tsuchimikado Shinto
It was founded by [[Abe no Seimei]] and influenced by [[:en:Onmyodo|Onmyodo]].<ref name="國學院大學テシタルミューシアム-2023a">{{Cite web |title=Encyclopedia of Shinto詳細 |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9907 |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=國學院大學デジタルミュージアム |language=ja}}</ref> in the 900s<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Cali |first1=Joseph |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=J1gEEAAAQBAJ&dq=tsuchimikado+shinto&pg=PA137 |title=Shinto Shrines: A Guide to the Sacred Sites of Japan's Ancient Religion |last2=Dougill |first2=John |date=30 November 2012 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-3775-4 |language=en}}</ref> It is highly linked to the [[Abe clan]].<ref name="國學院大學テシタルミューシアム-2023a" />
It is considered the modern form of Onmyodo.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Makoto |first=Hayashi |last2=Luers |first2=Dylan |last3=林淳 |date=2013 |title=The Development of Early Modern Onmyōdō |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/41955534 |journal=Japanese Journal of Religious Studies |volume=40 |issue=1 |pages=151–167 |issn=0304-1042}}</ref>
The current head is Yoshihito Fujita<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 October 2015 |title=天社土御門神道本庁 |url=https://japanese-religions.com/jr4210005008880/ |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=JAPANESE RELIGIONS |language=ja}}</ref>
It was banned by the {{interlanguage link|Tensha Shinto Prohibition Ordinance|ja|天社禁止令}}
Tsuchimikado Shintō was abolished in 1870 with the ban of [[Onmyōdō]], and only permitted again in 1945 with religious freedom and the abolition of [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]].<ref name="國學院大學テシタルミューシアム-2023a" /> A new organization was created for it in 1954.<ref>{{Cite web |title=備忘録 天社土御門神道 本庁 |url=http://kashomemorandum.blog.fc2.com/blog-entry-137.html |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=kashomemorandum.blog.fc2.com}}</ref>
==References== {{reflist}} {{Religious Confucianism}}
== Historical Background == The origins of Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto trace back to the [[Abe clan|Abe family]]'s establishment of Onmyōdō as a hereditary discipline focusing on {{ill|Astronomy|ja|天文道|1=Tenmondō (astrology)|lt=Tenmondō|qq= (astrology)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Astronomy|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmondō (astrology)|qq=}}, {{ill|Calendar Science|ja|暦道|1=Rekidō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Calendar Science|13=User:Immanuelle/Rekidō|qq=}}, and [[:en:Onmyōdō|Onmyōdō]] during the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]]. The family name "Tsuchimikado" was adopted after {{ill|Abe no Ariyo|ja|安倍有世|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe no Ariyo|qq=}} was granted the extraordinary court Rank of Junior Second Rank by [[:en:Ashikaga Yoshimitsu|Ashikaga Yoshimitsu]]. During the [[:en:Ōnin War|Ōnin War]], the family evacuated their estates in Kyoto and relocated to the Nata-shō area in [[:en:Wakasa Province|Wakasa Province]], where they were su11orted by local warlords such as the {{ill|Wakasa Takeda clan|ja|若狭武田氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakasa Takeda clan|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武田氏|1=Takeda clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1210114}}.
Despite this relocation, much of the Onmyōdō knowledge and practices maintained by the {{ill|Onmyōryō|ja|陰陽寮|1=Yin-Yang Bureau|2=ja|3=陰陽寮|4=fr|5=Bureau d'Onmyō|6=zh|7=阴阳寮|8=ko|9=음양료|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyōryō|13=User:Immanuelle/Yin-Yang Bureau|qq=}} were lost during the [[:en:Ōnin War|Ōnin War]]. Efforts were made to recover elements of Onmyōdō by incorporating practices from [[:en:Yoshida Shintō|Yoshida Shinto]] and elements influenced by esoteric Buddhism.
== Development into Tensha Shinto == Through the leadership of {{ill|Tsuchimikado Taifuku|ja|土御門泰福|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado Taifuku|1=Tsuchimikado Yasutomi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11423487}}, Tensha Shinto emerged as a synthesis of Onmyōdō, Yoshida Shinto practices, and Suika Shinto's Confucian-based teachings. Taifuku was a disciple of [[:en:Yamazaki Ansai|Yamazaki Ansai]], who emphasized reverence for the imperial lineage and divine sovereignty.
== Post-Meiji Restoration and Revival == With the [[Meiji Restoration]], Onmyōdō and Tensha Shinto were banned under the {{ill|Decree Prohibiting Tensha|ja|天社禁止令|1=Tensha Shinto Prohibition Ordinance|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Decree Prohibiting Tensha|13=User:Immanuelle/Tensha Shinto Prohibition Ordinance|qq=}} in 1870. The Tsuchimikado family ceased to engage in Onmyōdō practices, and the Tensha Shinto organization faced dissolution.
The revival of Tensha Shinto began in [[:en:Shōwa era|Shōwa period]] 29 (1954) with its incorporation as a religious corporation. Its headquarters was established in Fukui Prefecture, and the Fujita family assumed leadership roles.
== Current Status == Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto currently operates under the leadership of Fujita Yoshihito. The organization oversees several affiliated shrines and religious institutions. Efforts have been made to promote Tensha Shinto as part of local cultural heritage, su11orted by collaborations between academia, local governments, and private enterprises.

'''Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto''' (天社土御門神道, Tensha Tsuchimikado Shintō), or simply '''Tsuchimikado Shinto''' (土御門神道, Tsuchimikado Shintō), is a [[:en:Religious organization|Religious organization]] headquartered in [[Ōi Town]], [[Ōi District]], [[:en:Fukui Prefecture|Fukui Prefecture]] (formerly Nata-shō Village). The name "Tsuchimikado Shinto" is generally used, but it is also referred to as "Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto," incorporating the term "Tensha" from "Tensha Shrine" (天社宮), a shrine name bestowed by [[:en:Reigen Emperor|Reigen Emperor]] upon the Tsuchimikado family during the Edo period as the "Soke of Onmyōdō."
Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto is rooted in the [[Onmyōdō]] (yin-yang way) traditions passed down by the {{ill|Abe clan|ja|安倍氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe clan|qq=}}'s {{ill|Tsuchimikado clan|lt=Tsuchimikado clan|lt=Tsuchimikado family|ja|土御門家|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado family|qq=}}, descendants of [[Abe no Seimei]]. However, it evolved into "Tensha Shinto" by incorporating influences from [[:en:Yoshida Shinto|Yoshida Shinto]] in the medieval period and [[Suika Shinto]] proposed by the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] Shintoist and Confucian scholar [[:en:Yamazaki Ansai|Yamazaki Ansai]]. Strictly speaking, it is no longer purely Onmyōdō but is considered a Shinto-based organization{{efn2|While it is classified under "Miscellaneous Religions" in the religious corporation registry and not under [[:en:Sect Shinto|Sect Shinto]] or [[:en:Shrine Shinto|Shrine Shinto]].<ref name="nisino">[[#nisino|Nishino Shrine Journal]]</ref>}}. Currently, its leadership does not reside with the head of the Tsuchimikado family but rather with the Fujita family, which historically managed the household affairs of the Tsuchimikado family.
After the last Tsuchimikado family head, {{ill|Tsuchimikado Noriitada|ja|土御門範忠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado Noriitada|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135491517}} (1920–1994), passed away, the position of "Chief Priest" was abolished. Media and public relations are handled under the title "Leader of Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto Honcho" (庁長) or simply "Representative." The current highest-Ranking official (representative of the organization) holds the title "Honcho Leader."

However, it evolved into "Tensha Shinto" by incorporating influences from [[:en:Yoshida Shinto|Yoshida Shinto]] in the medieval period and [[Suika Shinto]] proposed by the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] Shintoist and Confucian scholar [[:en:Yamazaki Ansai|Yamazaki Ansai]]. Strictly speaking, it is no longer purely Onmyōdō but is considered a Shinto-based organization{{efn2|While it is classified under "Miscellaneous Religions" in the religious corporation registry and not under [[:en:Sect Shinto|Sect Shinto]] or [[:en:Shrine Shinto|Shrine Shinto]].<ref name="nisino">[[#nisino|Nishino Shrine Journal]]</ref>}}. Currently, its leadership does not reside with the head of the Tsuchimikado family but rather with the Fujita family, which historically managed the household affairs of the Tsuchimikado family.
After the last Tsuchimikado family head, {{ill|Tsuchimikado Noriitada|ja|土御門範忠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado Noriitada|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135491517}} (1920–1994), passed away, the position of "Chief Priest" was abolished. Media and public relations are handled under the title "Leader of Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto Honcho" (庁長) or simply "Representative." The current highest-Ranking official (representative of the organization) holds the title "Honcho Leader."
==Overview==
{{Short description|Shinto religious organization}} {{Use dmy dates|date=December 2023}}
{{Infobox organization | name = Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto | founder = [[Abe no Seimei]] | founding_location = Japan | website = https://onmyodo.jp }}
{{nihongo|'''Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto'''|天社土御門神道}}<ref>https://archive.today/uJNu5</ref> is a form of [[Confucian Shinto]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Encyclopedia of Shinto詳細 |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8943 |access-date=2023-03-10 |website=國學院大學デジタルミュージアム |language=ja}}</ref> It is also known as Tsuchimikado Shinto
It was founded by [[Abe no Seimei]] and influenced by [[:en:Onmyodo|Onmyodo]].<ref name="國學院大學テシタルミューシアム-2023a">{{Cite web |title=Encyclopedia of Shinto詳細 |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9907 |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=國學院大學デジタルミュージアム |language=ja}}</ref> in the 900s<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Cali |first1=Joseph |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=J1gEEAAAQBAJ&dq=tsuchimikado+shinto&pg=PA137 |title=Shinto Shrines: A Guide to the Sacred Sites of Japan's Ancient Religion |last2=Dougill |first2=John |date=30 November 2012 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-3775-4 |language=en}}</ref> It is highly linked to the [[Abe clan]].<ref name="國學院大學テシタルミューシアム-2023a" />
It is considered the modern form of Onmyodo.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Makoto |first=Hayashi |last2=Luers |first2=Dylan |last3=林淳 |date=2013 |title=The Development of Early Modern Onmyōdō |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/41955534 |journal=Japanese Journal of Religious Studies |volume=40 |issue=1 |pages=151–167 |issn=0304-1042}}</ref>
The current head is Yoshihito Fujita<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 October 2015 |title=天社土御門神道本庁 |url=https://japanese-religions.com/jr4210005008880/ |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=JAPANESE RELIGIONS |language=ja}}</ref>
It was banned by the {{interlanguage link|Tensha Shinto Prohibition Ordinance|ja|天社禁止令}}
Tsuchimikado Shintō was abolished in 1870 with the ban of [[Onmyōdō]], and only permitted again in 1945 with religious freedom and the abolition of [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]].<ref name="國學院大學テシタルミューシアム-2023a" /> A new organization was created for it in 1954.<ref>{{Cite web |title=備忘録 天社土御門神道 本庁 |url=http://kashomemorandum.blog.fc2.com/blog-entry-137.html |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=kashomemorandum.blog.fc2.com}}</ref>
==References== {{reflist}} {{Religious Confucianism}}
== Historical Background == The origins of Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto trace back to the [[Abe clan|Abe family]]'s establishment of Onmyōdō as a hereditary discipline focusing on {{ill|Astronomy|ja|天文道|1=Tenmondō (astrology)|lt=Tenmondō|qq= (astrology)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Astronomy|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmondō (astrology)|qq=}}, {{ill|Calendar Science|ja|暦道|1=Rekidō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Calendar Science|13=User:Immanuelle/Rekidō|qq=}}, and [[:en:Onmyōdō|Onmyōdō]] during the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]]. The family name "Tsuchimikado" was adopted after {{ill|Abe no Ariyo|ja|安倍有世|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe no Ariyo|qq=}} was granted the extraordinary court Rank of Junior Second Rank by [[:en:Ashikaga Yoshimitsu|Ashikaga Yoshimitsu]]. During the [[:en:Ōnin War|Ōnin War]], the family evacuated their estates in Kyoto and relocated to the Nata-shō area in [[:en:Wakasa Province|Wakasa Province]], where they were su11orted by local warlords such as the {{ill|Wakasa Takeda clan|ja|若狭武田氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakasa Takeda clan|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武田氏|1=Takeda clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1210114}}.
Despite this relocation, much of the Onmyōdō knowledge and practices maintained by the {{ill|Onmyōryō|ja|陰陽寮|1=Yin-Yang Bureau|2=ja|3=陰陽寮|4=fr|5=Bureau d'Onmyō|6=zh|7=阴阳寮|8=ko|9=음양료|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyōryō|13=User:Immanuelle/Yin-Yang Bureau|qq=}} were lost during the [[:en:Ōnin War|Ōnin War]]. Efforts were made to recover elements of Onmyōdō by incorporating practices from [[:en:Yoshida Shintō|Yoshida Shinto]] and elements influenced by esoteric Buddhism.
== Development into Tensha Shinto == Through the leadership of {{ill|Tsuchimikado Taifuku|ja|土御門泰福|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado Taifuku|1=Tsuchimikado Yasutomi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11423487}}, Tensha Shinto emerged as a synthesis of Onmyōdō, Yoshida Shinto practices, and Suika Shinto's Confucian-based teachings. Taifuku was a disciple of [[:en:Yamazaki Ansai|Yamazaki Ansai]], who emphasized reverence for the imperial lineage and divine sovereignty.
== Post-Meiji Restoration and Revival == With the [[Meiji Restoration]], Onmyōdō and Tensha Shinto were banned under the {{ill|Decree Prohibiting Tensha|ja|天社禁止令|1=Tensha Shinto Prohibition Ordinance|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Decree Prohibiting Tensha|13=User:Immanuelle/Tensha Shinto Prohibition Ordinance|qq=}} in 1870. The Tsuchimikado family ceased to engage in Onmyōdō practices, and the Tensha Shinto organization faced dissolution.
The revival of Tensha Shinto began in [[:en:Shōwa era|Shōwa period]] 29 (1954) with its incorporation as a religious corporation. Its headquarters was established in Fukui Prefecture, and the Fujita family assumed leadership roles.
== Current Status == Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto currently operates under the leadership of Fujita Yoshihito. The organization oversees several affiliated shrines and religious institutions. Efforts have been made to promote Tensha Shinto as part of local cultural heritage, su11orted by collaborations between academia, local governments, and private enterprises.

The name "Tsuchimikado Shinto" is generally used, but it is also referred to as "Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto," incorporating the term "Tensha" from "Tensha Shrine" (天社宮), a shrine name bestowed by [[:en:Reigen Emperor|Reigen Emperor]] upon the Tsuchimikado family during the Edo period as the "Soke of Onmyōdō."
Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto is rooted in the [[Onmyōdō]] (yin-yang way) traditions passed down by the {{ill|Abe clan|ja|安倍氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe clan|qq=}}'s {{ill|Tsuchimikado clan|lt=Tsuchimikado clan|lt=Tsuchimikado family|ja|土御門家|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado family|qq=}}, descendants of [[Abe no Seimei]]. However, it evolved into "Tensha Shinto" by incorporating influences from [[:en:Yoshida Shinto|Yoshida Shinto]] in the medieval period and [[Suika Shinto]] proposed by the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] Shintoist and Confucian scholar [[:en:Yamazaki Ansai|Yamazaki Ansai]]. Strictly speaking, it is no longer purely Onmyōdō but is considered a Shinto-based organization{{efn2|While it is classified under "Miscellaneous Religions" in the religious corporation registry and not under [[:en:Sect Shinto|Sect Shinto]] or [[:en:Shrine Shinto|Shrine Shinto]].<ref name="nisino">[[#nisino|Nishino Shrine Journal]]</ref>}}. Currently, its leadership does not reside with the head of the Tsuchimikado family but rather with the Fujita family, which historically managed the household affairs of the Tsuchimikado family.
After the last Tsuchimikado family head, {{ill|Tsuchimikado Noriitada|ja|土御門範忠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado Noriitada|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135491517}} (1920–1994), passed away, the position of "Chief Priest" was abolished. Media and public relations are handled under the title "Leader of Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto Honcho" (庁長) or simply "Representative." The current highest-Ranking official (representative of the organization) holds the title "Honcho Leader."
==Overview==
{{Short description|Shinto religious organization}} {{Use dmy dates|date=December 2023}}
{{Infobox organization | name = Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto | founder = [[Abe no Seimei]] | founding_location = Japan | website = https://onmyodo.jp }}
{{nihongo|'''Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto'''|天社土御門神道}}<ref>https://archive.today/uJNu5</ref> is a form of [[Confucian Shinto]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Encyclopedia of Shinto詳細 |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8943 |access-date=2023-03-10 |website=國學院大學デジタルミュージアム |language=ja}}</ref> It is also known as Tsuchimikado Shinto
It was founded by [[Abe no Seimei]] and influenced by [[:en:Onmyodo|Onmyodo]].<ref name="國學院大學テシタルミューシアム-2023a">{{Cite web |title=Encyclopedia of Shinto詳細 |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9907 |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=國學院大學デジタルミュージアム |language=ja}}</ref> in the 900s<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Cali |first1=Joseph |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=J1gEEAAAQBAJ&dq=tsuchimikado+shinto&pg=PA137 |title=Shinto Shrines: A Guide to the Sacred Sites of Japan's Ancient Religion |last2=Dougill |first2=John |date=30 November 2012 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-3775-4 |language=en}}</ref> It is highly linked to the [[Abe clan]].<ref name="國學院大學テシタルミューシアム-2023a" />
It is considered the modern form of Onmyodo.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Makoto |first=Hayashi |last2=Luers |first2=Dylan |last3=林淳 |date=2013 |title=The Development of Early Modern Onmyōdō |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/41955534 |journal=Japanese Journal of Religious Studies |volume=40 |issue=1 |pages=151–167 |issn=0304-1042}}</ref>
The current head is Yoshihito Fujita<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 October 2015 |title=天社土御門神道本庁 |url=https://japanese-religions.com/jr4210005008880/ |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=JAPANESE RELIGIONS |language=ja}}</ref>
It was banned by the {{interlanguage link|Tensha Shinto Prohibition Ordinance|ja|天社禁止令}}
Tsuchimikado Shintō was abolished in 1870 with the ban of [[Onmyōdō]], and only permitted again in 1945 with religious freedom and the abolition of [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]].<ref name="國學院大學テシタルミューシアム-2023a" /> A new organization was created for it in 1954.<ref>{{Cite web |title=備忘録 天社土御門神道 本庁 |url=http://kashomemorandum.blog.fc2.com/blog-entry-137.html |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=kashomemorandum.blog.fc2.com}}</ref>
==References== {{reflist}} {{Religious Confucianism}}
== Historical Background == The origins of Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto trace back to the [[Abe clan|Abe family]]'s establishment of Onmyōdō as a hereditary discipline focusing on {{ill|Astronomy|ja|天文道|1=Tenmondō (astrology)|lt=Tenmondō|qq= (astrology)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Astronomy|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmondō (astrology)|qq=}}, {{ill|Calendar Science|ja|暦道|1=Rekidō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Calendar Science|13=User:Immanuelle/Rekidō|qq=}}, and [[:en:Onmyōdō|Onmyōdō]] during the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]]. The family name "Tsuchimikado" was adopted after {{ill|Abe no Ariyo|ja|安倍有世|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe no Ariyo|qq=}} was granted the extraordinary court Rank of Junior Second Rank by [[:en:Ashikaga Yoshimitsu|Ashikaga Yoshimitsu]]. During the [[:en:Ōnin War|Ōnin War]], the family evacuated their estates in Kyoto and relocated to the Nata-shō area in [[:en:Wakasa Province|Wakasa Province]], where they were su11orted by local warlords such as the {{ill|Wakasa Takeda clan|ja|若狭武田氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakasa Takeda clan|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武田氏|1=Takeda clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1210114}}.
Despite this relocation, much of the Onmyōdō knowledge and practices maintained by the {{ill|Onmyōryō|ja|陰陽寮|1=Yin-Yang Bureau|2=ja|3=陰陽寮|4=fr|5=Bureau d'Onmyō|6=zh|7=阴阳寮|8=ko|9=음양료|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyōryō|13=User:Immanuelle/Yin-Yang Bureau|qq=}} were lost during the [[:en:Ōnin War|Ōnin War]]. Efforts were made to recover elements of Onmyōdō by incorporating practices from [[:en:Yoshida Shintō|Yoshida Shinto]] and elements influenced by esoteric Buddhism.
== Development into Tensha Shinto == Through the leadership of {{ill|Tsuchimikado Taifuku|ja|土御門泰福|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado Taifuku|1=Tsuchimikado Yasutomi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11423487}}, Tensha Shinto emerged as a synthesis of Onmyōdō, Yoshida Shinto practices, and Suika Shinto's Confucian-based teachings. Taifuku was a disciple of [[:en:Yamazaki Ansai|Yamazaki Ansai]], who emphasized reverence for the imperial lineage and divine sovereignty.
== Post-Meiji Restoration and Revival == With the [[Meiji Restoration]], Onmyōdō and Tensha Shinto were banned under the {{ill|Decree Prohibiting Tensha|ja|天社禁止令|1=Tensha Shinto Prohibition Ordinance|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Decree Prohibiting Tensha|13=User:Immanuelle/Tensha Shinto Prohibition Ordinance|qq=}} in 1870. The Tsuchimikado family ceased to engage in Onmyōdō practices, and the Tensha Shinto organization faced dissolution.
The revival of Tensha Shinto began in [[:en:Shōwa era|Shōwa period]] 29 (1954) with its incorporation as a religious corporation. Its headquarters was established in Fukui Prefecture, and the Fujita family assumed leadership roles.
== Current Status == Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto currently operates under the leadership of Fujita Yoshihito. The organization oversees several affiliated shrines and religious institutions. Efforts have been made to promote Tensha Shinto as part of local cultural heritage, su11orted by collaborations between academia, local governments, and private enterprises.

'''Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto''' (天社土御門神道, Tensha Tsuchimikado Shintō), or simply '''Tsuchimikado Shinto''' (土御門神道, Tsuchimikado Shintō), is a [[:en:Religious organization|Religious organization]] headquartered in [[Ōi Town]], [[Ōi District]], [[:en:Fukui Prefecture|Fukui Prefecture]] (formerly Nata-shō Village). The name "Tsuchimikado Shinto" is generally used, but it is also referred to as "Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto," incorporating the term "Tensha" from "Tensha Shrine" (天社宮), a shrine name bestowed by [[:en:Reigen Emperor|Reigen Emperor]] upon the Tsuchimikado family during the Edo period as the "Soke of Onmyōdō."
Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto is rooted in the [[Onmyōdō]] (yin-yang way) traditions passed down by the {{ill|Abe clan|ja|安倍氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe clan|qq=}}'s {{ill|Tsuchimikado clan|lt=Tsuchimikado clan|lt=Tsuchimikado family|ja|土御門家|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado family|qq=}}, descendants of [[Abe no Seimei]]. However, it evolved into "Tensha Shinto" by incorporating influences from [[:en:Yoshida Shinto|Yoshida Shinto]] in the medieval period and [[Suika Shinto]] proposed by the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] Shintoist and Confucian scholar [[:en:Yamazaki Ansai|Yamazaki Ansai]]. Strictly speaking, it is no longer purely Onmyōdō but is considered a Shinto-based organization{{efn2|While it is classified under "Miscellaneous Religions" in the religious corporation registry and not under [[:en:Sect Shinto|Sect Shinto]] or [[:en:Shrine Shinto|Shrine Shinto]].<ref name="nisino">[[#nisino|Nishino Shrine Journal]]</ref>}}. Currently, its leadership does not reside with the head of the Tsuchimikado family but rather with the Fujita family, which historically managed the household affairs of the Tsuchimikado family.
After the last Tsuchimikado family head, {{ill|Tsuchimikado Noriitada|ja|土御門範忠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado Noriitada|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135491517}} (1920–1994), passed away, the position of "Chief Priest" was abolished. Media and public relations are handled under the title "Leader of Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto Honcho" (庁長) or simply "Representative." The current highest-Ranking official (representative of the organization) holds the title "Honcho Leader."
==Overview==
{{Short description|Shinto religious organization}} {{Use dmy dates|date=December 2023}}
{{Infobox organization | name = Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto | founder = [[Abe no Seimei]] | founding_location = Japan | website = https://onmyodo.jp }}
{{nihongo|'''Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto'''|天社土御門神道}}<ref>https://archive.today/uJNu5</ref> is a form of [[Confucian Shinto]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Encyclopedia of Shinto詳細 |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8943 |access-date=2023-03-10 |website=國學院大學デジタルミュージアム |language=ja}}</ref> It is also known as Tsuchimikado Shinto
It was founded by [[Abe no Seimei]] and influenced by [[:en:Onmyodo|Onmyodo]].<ref name="國學院大學テシタルミューシアム-2023a">{{Cite web |title=Encyclopedia of Shinto詳細 |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9907 |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=國學院大學デジタルミュージアム |language=ja}}</ref> in the 900s<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Cali |first1=Joseph |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=J1gEEAAAQBAJ&dq=tsuchimikado+shinto&pg=PA137 |title=Shinto Shrines: A Guide to the Sacred Sites of Japan's Ancient Religion |last2=Dougill |first2=John |date=30 November 2012 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-3775-4 |language=en}}</ref> It is highly linked to the [[Abe clan]].<ref name="國學院大學テシタルミューシアム-2023a" />
It is considered the modern form of Onmyodo.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Makoto |first=Hayashi |last2=Luers |first2=Dylan |last3=林淳 |date=2013 |title=The Development of Early Modern Onmyōdō |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/41955534 |journal=Japanese Journal of Religious Studies |volume=40 |issue=1 |pages=151–167 |issn=0304-1042}}</ref>
The current head is Yoshihito Fujita<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 October 2015 |title=天社土御門神道本庁 |url=https://japanese-religions.com/jr4210005008880/ |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=JAPANESE RELIGIONS |language=ja}}</ref>
It was banned by the {{interlanguage link|Tensha Shinto Prohibition Ordinance|ja|天社禁止令}}
Tsuchimikado Shintō was abolished in 1870 with the ban of [[Onmyōdō]], and only permitted again in 1945 with religious freedom and the abolition of [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]].<ref name="國學院大學テシタルミューシアム-2023a" /> A new organization was created for it in 1954.<ref>{{Cite web |title=備忘録 天社土御門神道 本庁 |url=http://kashomemorandum.blog.fc2.com/blog-entry-137.html |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=kashomemorandum.blog.fc2.com}}</ref>
==References== {{reflist}} {{Religious Confucianism}}
== Historical Background == The origins of Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto trace back to the [[Abe clan|Abe family]]'s establishment of Onmyōdō as a hereditary discipline focusing on {{ill|Astronomy|ja|天文道|1=Tenmondō (astrology)|lt=Tenmondō|qq= (astrology)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Astronomy|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmondō (astrology)|qq=}}, {{ill|Calendar Science|ja|暦道|1=Rekidō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Calendar Science|13=User:Immanuelle/Rekidō|qq=}}, and [[:en:Onmyōdō|Onmyōdō]] during the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]]. The family name "Tsuchimikado" was adopted after {{ill|Abe no Ariyo|ja|安倍有世|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe no Ariyo|qq=}} was granted the extraordinary court Rank of Junior Second Rank by [[:en:Ashikaga Yoshimitsu|Ashikaga Yoshimitsu]]. During the [[:en:Ōnin War|Ōnin War]], the family evacuated their estates in Kyoto and relocated to the Nata-shō area in [[:en:Wakasa Province|Wakasa Province]], where they were su11orted by local warlords such as the {{ill|Wakasa Takeda clan|ja|若狭武田氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakasa Takeda clan|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武田氏|1=Takeda clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1210114}}.
Despite this relocation, much of the Onmyōdō knowledge and practices maintained by the {{ill|Onmyōryō|ja|陰陽寮|1=Yin-Yang Bureau|2=ja|3=陰陽寮|4=fr|5=Bureau d'Onmyō|6=zh|7=阴阳寮|8=ko|9=음양료|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyōryō|13=User:Immanuelle/Yin-Yang Bureau|qq=}} were lost during the [[:en:Ōnin War|Ōnin War]]. Efforts were made to recover elements of Onmyōdō by incorporating practices from [[:en:Yoshida Shintō|Yoshida Shinto]] and elements influenced by esoteric Buddhism.
== Development into Tensha Shinto == Through the leadership of {{ill|Tsuchimikado Taifuku|ja|土御門泰福|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado Taifuku|1=Tsuchimikado Yasutomi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11423487}}, Tensha Shinto emerged as a synthesis of Onmyōdō, Yoshida Shinto practices, and Suika Shinto's Confucian-based teachings. Taifuku was a disciple of [[:en:Yamazaki Ansai|Yamazaki Ansai]], who emphasized reverence for the imperial lineage and divine sovereignty.
== Post-Meiji Restoration and Revival == With the [[Meiji Restoration]], Onmyōdō and Tensha Shinto were banned under the {{ill|Decree Prohibiting Tensha|ja|天社禁止令|1=Tensha Shinto Prohibition Ordinance|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Decree Prohibiting Tensha|13=User:Immanuelle/Tensha Shinto Prohibition Ordinance|qq=}} in 1870. The Tsuchimikado family ceased to engage in Onmyōdō practices, and the Tensha Shinto organization faced dissolution.
The revival of Tensha Shinto began in [[:en:Shōwa era|Shōwa period]] 29 (1954) with its incorporation as a religious corporation. Its headquarters was established in Fukui Prefecture, and the Fujita family assumed leadership roles.
== Current Status == Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto currently operates under the leadership of Fujita Yoshihito. The organization oversees several affiliated shrines and religious institutions. Efforts have been made to promote Tensha Shinto as part of local cultural heritage, su11orted by collaborations between academia, local governments, and private enterprises.

'''Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto''' (天社土御門神道, Tensha Tsuchimikado Shintō), or simply '''Tsuchimikado Shinto''' (土御門神道, Tsuchimikado Shintō), is a [[:en:Religious organization|Religious organization]] headquartered in [[Ōi Town]], [[Ōi District]], [[:en:Fukui Prefecture|Fukui Prefecture]] (formerly Nata-shō Village). The name "Tsuchimikado Shinto" is generally used, but it is also referred to as "Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto," incorporating the term "Tensha" from "Tensha Shrine" (天社宮), a shrine name bestowed by [[:en:Reigen Emperor|Reigen Emperor]] upon the Tsuchimikado family during the Edo period as the "Soke of Onmyōdō."
Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto is rooted in the [[Onmyōdō]] (yin-yang way) traditions passed down by the {{ill|Abe clan|ja|安倍氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe clan|qq=}}'s {{ill|Tsuchimikado clan|lt=Tsuchimikado clan|lt=Tsuchimikado family|ja|土御門家|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado family|qq=}}, descendants of [[Abe no Seimei]]. However, it evolved into "Tensha Shinto" by incorporating influences from [[:en:Yoshida Shinto|Yoshida Shinto]] in the medieval period and [[Suika Shinto]] proposed by the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] Shintoist and Confucian scholar [[:en:Yamazaki Ansai|Yamazaki Ansai]]. Strictly speaking, it is no longer purely Onmyōdō but is considered a Shinto-based organization{{efn2|While it is classified under "Miscellaneous Religions" in the religious corporation registry and not under [[:en:Sect Shinto|Sect Shinto]] or [[:en:Shrine Shinto|Shrine Shinto]].<ref name="nisino">[[#nisino|Nishino Shrine Journal]]</ref>}}. Currently, its leadership does not reside with the head of the Tsuchimikado family but rather with the Fujita family, which historically managed the household affairs of the Tsuchimikado family.
After the last Tsuchimikado family head, {{ill|Tsuchimikado Noriitada|ja|土御門範忠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado Noriitada|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135491517}} (1920–1994), passed away, the position of "Chief Priest" was abolished. Media and public relations are handled under the title "Leader of Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto Honcho" (庁長) or simply "Representative." The current highest-Ranking official (representative of the organization) holds the title "Honcho Leader."
==Overview==
{{Short description|Shinto religious organization}} {{Use dmy dates|date=December 2023}}
{{Infobox organization | name = Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto | founder = [[Abe no Seimei]] | founding_location = Japan | website = https://onmyodo.jp }}
{{nihongo|'''Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto'''|天社土御門神道}}<ref>https://archive.today/uJNu5</ref> is a form of [[Confucian Shinto]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Encyclopedia of Shinto詳細 |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8943 |access-date=2023-03-10 |website=國學院大學デジタルミュージアム |language=ja}}</ref> It is also known as Tsuchimikado Shinto
It was founded by [[Abe no Seimei]] and influenced by [[:en:Onmyodo|Onmyodo]].<ref name="國學院大學テシタルミューシアム-2023a">{{Cite web |title=Encyclopedia of Shinto詳細 |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9907 |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=國學院大學デジタルミュージアム |language=ja}}</ref> in the 900s<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Cali |first1=Joseph |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=J1gEEAAAQBAJ&dq=tsuchimikado+shinto&pg=PA137 |title=Shinto Shrines: A Guide to the Sacred Sites of Japan's Ancient Religion |last2=Dougill |first2=John |date=30 November 2012 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-3775-4 |language=en}}</ref> It is highly linked to the [[Abe clan]].<ref name="國學院大學テシタルミューシアム-2023a" />
It is considered the modern form of Onmyodo.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Makoto |first=Hayashi |last2=Luers |first2=Dylan |last3=林淳 |date=2013 |title=The Development of Early Modern Onmyōdō |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/41955534 |journal=Japanese Journal of Religious Studies |volume=40 |issue=1 |pages=151–167 |issn=0304-1042}}</ref>
The current head is Yoshihito Fujita<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 October 2015 |title=天社土御門神道本庁 |url=https://japanese-religions.com/jr4210005008880/ |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=JAPANESE RELIGIONS |language=ja}}</ref>
It was banned by the {{interlanguage link|Tensha Shinto Prohibition Ordinance|ja|天社禁止令}}
Tsuchimikado Shintō was abolished in 1870 with the ban of [[Onmyōdō]], and only permitted again in 1945 with religious freedom and the abolition of [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]].<ref name="國學院大學テシタルミューシアム-2023a" /> A new organization was created for it in 1954.<ref>{{Cite web |title=備忘録 天社土御門神道 本庁 |url=http://kashomemorandum.blog.fc2.com/blog-entry-137.html |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=kashomemorandum.blog.fc2.com}}</ref>

== Historical Background == The origins of Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto trace back to the [[Abe clan|Abe family]]'s establishment of Onmyōdō as a hereditary discipline focusing on {{ill|Astronomy|ja|天文道|1=Tenmondō (astrology)|lt=Tenmondō|qq= (astrology)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Astronomy|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmondō (astrology)|qq=}}, {{ill|Calendar Science|ja|暦道|1=Rekidō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Calendar Science|13=User:Immanuelle/Rekidō|qq=}}, and [[:en:Onmyōdō|Onmyōdō]] during the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]]. The family name "Tsuchimikado" was adopted after {{ill|Abe no Ariyo|ja|安倍有世|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe no Ariyo|qq=}} was granted the extraordinary court Rank of Junior Second Rank by [[:en:Ashikaga Yoshimitsu|Ashikaga Yoshimitsu]]. During the [[:en:Ōnin War|Ōnin War]], the family evacuated their estates in Kyoto and relocated to the Nata-shō area in [[:en:Wakasa Province|Wakasa Province]], where they were su11orted by local warlords such as the {{ill|Wakasa Takeda clan|ja|若狭武田氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakasa Takeda clan|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武田氏|1=Takeda clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1210114}}.
Despite this relocation, much of the Onmyōdō knowledge and practices maintained by the {{ill|Onmyōryō|ja|陰陽寮|1=Yin-Yang Bureau|2=ja|3=陰陽寮|4=fr|5=Bureau d'Onmyō|6=zh|7=阴阳寮|8=ko|9=음양료|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyōryō|13=User:Immanuelle/Yin-Yang Bureau|qq=}} were lost during the [[:en:Ōnin War|Ōnin War]]. Efforts were made to recover elements of Onmyōdō by incorporating practices from [[:en:Yoshida Shintō|Yoshida Shinto]] and elements influenced by esoteric Buddhism.
== Development into Tensha Shinto == Through the leadership of {{ill|Tsuchimikado Taifuku|ja|土御門泰福|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado Taifuku|1=Tsuchimikado Yasutomi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11423487}}, Tensha Shinto emerged as a synthesis of Onmyōdō, Yoshida Shinto practices, and Suika Shinto's Confucian-based teachings. Taifuku was a disciple of [[:en:Yamazaki Ansai|Yamazaki Ansai]], who emphasized reverence for the imperial lineage and divine sovereignty.
== Post-Meiji Restoration and Revival == With the [[Meiji Restoration]], Onmyōdō and Tensha Shinto were banned under the {{ill|Decree Prohibiting Tensha|ja|天社禁止令|1=Tensha Shinto Prohibition Ordinance|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Decree Prohibiting Tensha|13=User:Immanuelle/Tensha Shinto Prohibition Ordinance|qq=}} in 1870. The Tsuchimikado family ceased to engage in Onmyōdō practices, and the Tensha Shinto organization faced dissolution.
The revival of Tensha Shinto began in [[:en:Shōwa era|Shōwa period]] 29 (1954) with its incorporation as a religious corporation. Its headquarters was established in Fukui Prefecture, and the Fujita family assumed leadership roles.
== Current Status == Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto currently operates under the leadership of Fujita Yoshihito. The organization oversees several affiliated shrines and religious institutions. Efforts have been made to promote Tensha Shinto as part of local cultural heritage, su11orted by collaborations between academia, local governments, and private enterprises.

Efforts have been made to promote Tensha Shinto as part of local cultural heritage, su11orted by collaborations between academia, local governments, and private enterprises.

{{Unreferenced|date=October 8, 2019 (Tuesday)}} {{Infobox Organization | Name = Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto Honcho | image = | image size = | Caption = | Established = [[:en:1954|1954]] (January 11) | Type = {{ill|Religious Corporation|ja|宗教法人|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Religious Corporation|1=religious corporation|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q7311343}} | Status = {{ill|Incorporated religious corporation under the jurisdiction of the Minister of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology|ja|文部科学大臣所轄包括宗教法人|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Incorporated religious corporation under the jurisdiction of the Minister of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} | Headquarters = 129-9, Nadajō, Nata-shō, Ōi Town, Ōi District, Fukui Prefecture | Founder = {{ill|Tsuchimikado Noriitada|ja|土御門範忠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado Noriitada|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135491517}} | President = Fujita Yuji (Honcho Leader) | People = {{ill|Tsuchimikado Noriitada|ja|土御門範忠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado Noriitada|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135491517}}, {{ill|Fujita Kando|ja|藤田乾堂|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujita Kando|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} | Website = https://onmyodo.jp | Remarks = }}
'''Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto''' (天社土御門神道, Tensha Tsuchimikado Shintō), or simply '''Tsuchimikado Shinto''' (土御門神道, Tsuchimikado Shintō), is a [[:en:Religious organization|Religious organization]] headquartered in [[Ōi Town]], [[Ōi District]], [[:en:Fukui Prefecture|Fukui Prefecture]] (formerly Nata-shō Village). The name "Tsuchimikado Shinto" is generally used, but it is also referred to as "Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto," incorporating the term "Tensha" from "Tensha Shrine" (天社宮), a shrine name bestowed by [[:en:Reigen Emperor|Reigen Emperor]] upon the Tsuchimikado family during the Edo period as the "Soke of Onmyōdō."
Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto is rooted in the [[Onmyōdō]] (yin-yang way) traditions passed down by the {{ill|Abe clan|ja|安倍氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe clan|qq=}}'s {{ill|Tsuchimikado clan|lt=Tsuchimikado clan|lt=Tsuchimikado family|ja|土御門家|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado family|qq=}}, descendants of [[Abe no Seimei]]. However, it evolved into "Tensha Shinto" by incorporating influences from [[:en:Yoshida Shinto|Yoshida Shinto]] in the medieval period and [[Suika Shinto]] proposed by the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] Shintoist and Confucian scholar [[:en:Yamazaki Ansai|Yamazaki Ansai]]. Strictly speaking, it is no longer purely Onmyōdō but is considered a Shinto-based organization{{efn2|While it is classified under "Miscellaneous Religions" in the religious corporation registry and not under [[:en:Sect Shinto|Sect Shinto]] or [[:en:Shrine Shinto|Shrine Shinto]].<ref name="nisino">[[#nisino|Nishino Shrine Journal]]</ref>}}. Currently, its leadership does not reside with the head of the Tsuchimikado family but rather with the Fujita family, which historically managed the household affairs of the Tsuchimikado family.
After the last Tsuchimikado family head, {{ill|Tsuchimikado Noriitada|ja|土御門範忠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado Noriitada|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135491517}} (1920–1994), passed away, the position of "Chief Priest" was abolished. Media and public relations are handled under the title "Leader of Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto Honcho" (庁長) or simply "Representative." The current highest-Ranking official (representative of the organization) holds the title "Honcho Leader."
==Overview==
{{Short description|Shinto religious organization}} {{Use dmy dates|date=December 2023}}
{{Infobox organization | name = Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto | founder = [[Abe no Seimei]] | founding_location = Japan | website = https://onmyodo.jp }}
{{nihongo|'''Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto'''|天社土御門神道}}<ref>https://archive.today/uJNu5</ref> is a form of [[Confucian Shinto]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Encyclopedia of Shinto詳細 |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8943 |access-date=2023-03-10 |website=國學院大學デジタルミュージアム |language=ja}}</ref> It is also known as Tsuchimikado Shinto
It was founded by [[Abe no Seimei]] and influenced by [[:en:Onmyodo|Onmyodo]].<ref name="國學院大學テシタルミューシアム-2023a">{{Cite web |title=Encyclopedia of Shinto詳細 |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9907 |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=國學院大學デジタルミュージアム |language=ja}}</ref> in the 900s<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Cali |first1=Joseph |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=J1gEEAAAQBAJ&dq=tsuchimikado+shinto&pg=PA137 |title=Shinto Shrines: A Guide to the Sacred Sites of Japan's Ancient Religion |last2=Dougill |first2=John |date=30 November 2012 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-3775-4 |language=en}}</ref> It is highly linked to the [[Abe clan]].<ref name="國學院大學テシタルミューシアム-2023a" />
It is considered the modern form of Onmyodo.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Makoto |first=Hayashi |last2=Luers |first2=Dylan |last3=林淳 |date=2013 |title=The Development of Early Modern Onmyōdō |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/41955534 |journal=Japanese Journal of Religious Studies |volume=40 |issue=1 |pages=151–167 |issn=0304-1042}}</ref>
The current head is Yoshihito Fujita<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 October 2015 |title=天社土御門神道本庁 |url=https://japanese-religions.com/jr4210005008880/ |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=JAPANESE RELIGIONS |language=ja}}</ref>
It was banned by the {{interlanguage link|Tensha Shinto Prohibition Ordinance|ja|天社禁止令}}
Tsuchimikado Shintō was abolished in 1870 with the ban of [[Onmyōdō]], and only permitted again in 1945 with religious freedom and the abolition of [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]].<ref name="國學院大學テシタルミューシアム-2023a" /> A new organization was created for it in 1954.<ref>{{Cite web |title=備忘録 天社土御門神道 本庁 |url=http://kashomemorandum.blog.fc2.com/blog-entry-137.html |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=kashomemorandum.blog.fc2.com}}</ref>
==References== {{reflist}} {{Religious Confucianism}}
== Historical Background == The origins of Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto trace back to the [[Abe clan|Abe family]]'s establishment of Onmyōdō as a hereditary discipline focusing on {{ill|Astronomy|ja|天文道|1=Tenmondō (astrology)|lt=Tenmondō|qq= (astrology)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Astronomy|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmondō (astrology)|qq=}}, {{ill|Calendar Science|ja|暦道|1=Rekidō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Calendar Science|13=User:Immanuelle/Rekidō|qq=}}, and [[:en:Onmyōdō|Onmyōdō]] during the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]]. The family name "Tsuchimikado" was adopted after {{ill|Abe no Ariyo|ja|安倍有世|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe no Ariyo|qq=}} was granted the extraordinary court Rank of Junior Second Rank by [[:en:Ashikaga Yoshimitsu|Ashikaga Yoshimitsu]]. During the [[:en:Ōnin War|Ōnin War]], the family evacuated their estates in Kyoto and relocated to the Nata-shō area in [[:en:Wakasa Province|Wakasa Province]], where they were su11orted by local warlords such as the {{ill|Wakasa Takeda clan|ja|若狭武田氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakasa Takeda clan|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武田氏|1=Takeda clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1210114}}.
Despite this relocation, much of the Onmyōdō knowledge and practices maintained by the {{ill|Onmyōryō|ja|陰陽寮|1=Yin-Yang Bureau|2=ja|3=陰陽寮|4=fr|5=Bureau d'Onmyō|6=zh|7=阴阳寮|8=ko|9=음양료|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyōryō|13=User:Immanuelle/Yin-Yang Bureau|qq=}} were lost during the [[:en:Ōnin War|Ōnin War]]. Efforts were made to recover elements of Onmyōdō by incorporating practices from [[:en:Yoshida Shintō|Yoshida Shinto]] and elements influenced by esoteric Buddhism.
== Development into Tensha Shinto == Through the leadership of {{ill|Tsuchimikado Taifuku|ja|土御門泰福|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado Taifuku|1=Tsuchimikado Yasutomi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11423487}}, Tensha Shinto emerged as a synthesis of Onmyōdō, Yoshida Shinto practices, and Suika Shinto's Confucian-based teachings. Taifuku was a disciple of [[:en:Yamazaki Ansai|Yamazaki Ansai]], who emphasized reverence for the imperial lineage and divine sovereignty.
== Post-Meiji Restoration and Revival == With the [[Meiji Restoration]], Onmyōdō and Tensha Shinto were banned under the {{ill|Decree Prohibiting Tensha|ja|天社禁止令|1=Tensha Shinto Prohibition Ordinance|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Decree Prohibiting Tensha|13=User:Immanuelle/Tensha Shinto Prohibition Ordinance|qq=}} in 1870. The Tsuchimikado family ceased to engage in Onmyōdō practices, and the Tensha Shinto organization faced dissolution.
The revival of Tensha Shinto began in [[:en:Shōwa era|Shōwa period]] 29 (1954) with its incorporation as a religious corporation. Its headquarters was established in Fukui Prefecture, and the Fujita family assumed leadership roles.
== Current Status == Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto currently operates under the leadership of Fujita Yoshihito. The organization oversees several affiliated shrines and religious institutions. Efforts have been made to promote Tensha Shinto as part of local cultural heritage, su11orted by collaborations between academia, local governments, and private enterprises.

== Post-Meiji Restoration and Revival == With the [[Meiji Restoration]], Onmyōdō and Tensha Shinto were banned under the {{ill|Decree Prohibiting Tensha|ja|天社禁止令|1=Tensha Shinto Prohibition Ordinance|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Decree Prohibiting Tensha|13=User:Immanuelle/Tensha Shinto Prohibition Ordinance|qq=}} in 1870. The Tsuchimikado family ceased to engage in Onmyōdō practices, and the Tensha Shinto organization faced dissolution.
The revival of Tensha Shinto began in [[:en:Shōwa era|Shōwa period]] 29 (1954) with its incorporation as a religious corporation. Its headquarters was established in Fukui Prefecture, and the Fujita family assumed leadership roles.
== Current Status == Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto currently operates under the leadership of Fujita Yoshihito. The organization oversees several affiliated shrines and religious institutions. Efforts have been made to promote Tensha Shinto as part of local cultural heritage, su11orted by collaborations between academia, local governments, and private enterprises.

'''Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto''' (天社土御門神道, Tensha Tsuchimikado Shintō), or simply '''Tsuchimikado Shinto''' (土御門神道, Tsuchimikado Shintō), is a [[:en:Religious organization|Religious organization]] headquartered in [[Ōi Town]], [[Ōi District]], [[:en:Fukui Prefecture|Fukui Prefecture]] (formerly Nata-shō Village). The name "Tsuchimikado Shinto" is generally used, but it is also referred to as "Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto," incorporating the term "Tensha" from "Tensha Shrine" (天社宮), a shrine name bestowed by [[:en:Reigen Emperor|Reigen Emperor]] upon the Tsuchimikado family during the Edo period as the "Soke of Onmyōdō."
Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto is rooted in the [[Onmyōdō]] (yin-yang way) traditions passed down by the {{ill|Abe clan|ja|安倍氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe clan|qq=}}'s {{ill|Tsuchimikado clan|lt=Tsuchimikado clan|lt=Tsuchimikado family|ja|土御門家|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado family|qq=}}, descendants of [[Abe no Seimei]]. However, it evolved into "Tensha Shinto" by incorporating influences from [[:en:Yoshida Shinto|Yoshida Shinto]] in the medieval period and [[Suika Shinto]] proposed by the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] Shintoist and Confucian scholar [[:en:Yamazaki Ansai|Yamazaki Ansai]]. Strictly speaking, it is no longer purely Onmyōdō but is considered a Shinto-based organization{{efn2|While it is classified under "Miscellaneous Religions" in the religious corporation registry and not under [[:en:Sect Shinto|Sect Shinto]] or [[:en:Shrine Shinto|Shrine Shinto]].<ref name="nisino">[[#nisino|Nishino Shrine Journal]]</ref>}}. Currently, its leadership does not reside with the head of the Tsuchimikado family but rather with the Fujita family, which historically managed the household affairs of the Tsuchimikado family.
After the last Tsuchimikado family head, {{ill|Tsuchimikado Noriitada|ja|土御門範忠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado Noriitada|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135491517}} (1920–1994), passed away, the position of "Chief Priest" was abolished. Media and public relations are handled under the title "Leader of Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto Honcho" (庁長) or simply "Representative." The current highest-Ranking official (representative of the organization) holds the title "Honcho Leader."
==Overview==
{{Short description|Shinto religious organization}} {{Use dmy dates|date=December 2023}}
{{Infobox organization | name = Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto | founder = [[Abe no Seimei]] | founding_location = Japan | website = https://onmyodo.jp }}
{{nihongo|'''Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto'''|天社土御門神道}}<ref>https://archive.today/uJNu5</ref> is a form of [[Confucian Shinto]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Encyclopedia of Shinto詳細 |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8943 |access-date=2023-03-10 |website=國學院大學デジタルミュージアム |language=ja}}</ref> It is also known as Tsuchimikado Shinto
It was founded by [[Abe no Seimei]] and influenced by [[:en:Onmyodo|Onmyodo]].<ref name="國學院大學テシタルミューシアム-2023a">{{Cite web |title=Encyclopedia of Shinto詳細 |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9907 |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=國學院大學デジタルミュージアム |language=ja}}</ref> in the 900s<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Cali |first1=Joseph |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=J1gEEAAAQBAJ&dq=tsuchimikado+shinto&pg=PA137 |title=Shinto Shrines: A Guide to the Sacred Sites of Japan's Ancient Religion |last2=Dougill |first2=John |date=30 November 2012 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-3775-4 |language=en}}</ref> It is highly linked to the [[Abe clan]].<ref name="國學院大學テシタルミューシアム-2023a" />
It is considered the modern form of Onmyodo.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Makoto |first=Hayashi |last2=Luers |first2=Dylan |last3=林淳 |date=2013 |title=The Development of Early Modern Onmyōdō |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/41955534 |journal=Japanese Journal of Religious Studies |volume=40 |issue=1 |pages=151–167 |issn=0304-1042}}</ref>
The current head is Yoshihito Fujita<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 October 2015 |title=天社土御門神道本庁 |url=https://japanese-religions.com/jr4210005008880/ |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=JAPANESE RELIGIONS |language=ja}}</ref>
It was banned by the {{interlanguage link|Tensha Shinto Prohibition Ordinance|ja|天社禁止令}}
Tsuchimikado Shintō was abolished in 1870 with the ban of [[Onmyōdō]], and only permitted again in 1945 with religious freedom and the abolition of [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]].<ref name="國學院大學テシタルミューシアム-2023a" /> A new organization was created for it in 1954.<ref>{{Cite web |title=備忘録 天社土御門神道 本庁 |url=http://kashomemorandum.blog.fc2.com/blog-entry-137.html |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=kashomemorandum.blog.fc2.com}}</ref>

== Historical Background == The origins of Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto trace back to the [[Abe clan|Abe family]]'s establishment of Onmyōdō as a hereditary discipline focusing on {{ill|Astronomy|ja|天文道|1=Tenmondō (astrology)|lt=Tenmondō|qq= (astrology)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Astronomy|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmondō (astrology)|qq=}}, {{ill|Calendar Science|ja|暦道|1=Rekidō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Calendar Science|13=User:Immanuelle/Rekidō|qq=}}, and [[:en:Onmyōdō|Onmyōdō]] during the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]]. The family name "Tsuchimikado" was adopted after {{ill|Abe no Ariyo|ja|安倍有世|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe no Ariyo|qq=}} was granted the extraordinary court Rank of Junior Second Rank by [[:en:Ashikaga Yoshimitsu|Ashikaga Yoshimitsu]]. During the [[:en:Ōnin War|Ōnin War]], the family evacuated their estates in Kyoto and relocated to the Nata-shō area in [[:en:Wakasa Province|Wakasa Province]], where they were su11orted by local warlords such as the {{ill|Wakasa Takeda clan|ja|若狭武田氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakasa Takeda clan|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武田氏|1=Takeda clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1210114}}.
Despite this relocation, much of the Onmyōdō knowledge and practices maintained by the {{ill|Onmyōryō|ja|陰陽寮|1=Yin-Yang Bureau|2=ja|3=陰陽寮|4=fr|5=Bureau d'Onmyō|6=zh|7=阴阳寮|8=ko|9=음양료|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyōryō|13=User:Immanuelle/Yin-Yang Bureau|qq=}} were lost during the [[:en:Ōnin War|Ōnin War]]. Efforts were made to recover elements of Onmyōdō by incorporating practices from [[:en:Yoshida Shintō|Yoshida Shinto]] and elements influenced by esoteric Buddhism.
== Development into Tensha Shinto == Through the leadership of {{ill|Tsuchimikado Taifuku|ja|土御門泰福|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado Taifuku|1=Tsuchimikado Yasutomi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11423487}}, Tensha Shinto emerged as a synthesis of Onmyōdō, Yoshida Shinto practices, and Suika Shinto's Confucian-based teachings. The Tsuchimikado family ceased to engage in Onmyōdō practices, and the Tensha Shinto organization faced dissolution.
The revival of Tensha Shinto began in [[:en:Shōwa era|Shōwa period]] 29 (1954) with its incorporation as a religious corporation. Its headquarters was established in Fukui Prefecture, and the Fujita family assumed leadership roles.
== Current Status == Tensha Tsuchimikado Shinto currently operates under the leadership of Fujita Yoshihito. The organization oversees several affiliated shrines and religious institutions. Efforts have been made to promote Tensha Shinto as part of local cultural heritage, su11orted by collaborations between academia, local governments, and private enterprises.
